name: PreCalculatedPrimeTable::CalculatePrimesUpTo
prose: Private member PreCalculatedPrimeTable::CalculatePrimesUpTo(int max): a sieve of Eratosthenes over the is_prime_ array. Precondition: is_prime_ points to a writable array of is_prime_size_ bools with is_prime_size_ >= 2 (the code writes is_prime_[0] and is_prime_[1]), 0 <= max < is_prime_size_, and max < 2147302921 (46339*46339): the loop variable i takes the values 2, 3, 5, 7, ... (i += i % 2 + 1), so i can reach 46341 whenever 46339*46339 <= max, and the test i * i <= max then overflows int. Postcondition: fills the whole array with true, sets is_prime_[0] and is_prime_[1] to false, and for each i in that sequence with i*i <= max and is_prime_[i] still true sets is_prime_[j] = false for j = i*i, i*i+i, ... up to max. On return, for 0 <= k <= max is_prime_[k] is true exactly when k is prime, and entries with max < k < is_prime_size_ stay true. No value is returned and nothing outside the array is modified.
note: reviewer RIGHT: i reaches 46341 (46341^2 > INT_MAX) when max >= 46339^2, so the bound is 46339^2 not 46340^2; also verified odd composites i are skipped via is_prime_[i] check (lines 100-116)

name: PreCalculatedPrimeTable::PreCalculatedPrimeTable
prose: Explicit constructor PreCalculatedPrimeTable(int max) (lines 80-84). Precondition: 1 <= max < 2147302921 (46339*46339): for max <= 0 is_prime_size_ becomes 1 and CalculatePrimesUpTo(0) writes is_prime_[1], one element past the end of the 1-element array; for larger max the sieve in CalculatePrimesUpTo overflows int (see that function). The new bool[] allocation may throw std::bad_alloc. Postcondition: is_prime_size_ == max(1, max + 1) (== max + 1 for the allowed range), is_prime_ points to a new[]-allocated array of that many bools, and CalculatePrimesUpTo(is_prime_size_ - 1) has been run so that is_prime_[k] is true exactly when k is prime for 0 <= k < is_prime_size_. The destructor releases the array with delete[].
note: reviewer RIGHT: bound is 46339^2 (sieve i reaches 46341); additionally max<=0 gives size 1 and an out-of-bounds write to is_prime_[1]

name: WindowsDeathTest::AssumeRole
prose: DeathTest::TestRole WindowsDeathTest::AssumeRole() (gtest-death-test.cc lines 746-829; slice cut the head). Precondition: Google Test's unit-test machinery is initialised (GetUnitTestImpl(), impl->current_test_info() non-null, UnitTest::GetInstance()->original_working_dir() valid). Postcondition: if impl->internal_run_death_test_flag() is non-null (this is the child), it only calls set_write_fd(flag->write_fd()) and returns EXECUTE_TEST. Otherwise (parent) it creates an inheritable anonymous pipe with CreatePipe, stores the read end as a descriptor via set_read_fd(_open_osfhandle(...)) (the result is not checked) and the write end in write_handle_, creates an unnamed inheritable event stored in event_handle_, builds a --gtest_filter flag and a --gtest_internal_run_death_test flag (file, line, death test index, current process id, write handle value, event handle value), gets the module file name into a char[_MAX_PATH + 1] buffer by passing size _MAX_PATH, clears DeathTest's last death test message, starts CaptureStderr(), calls FlushInfoLog(), and calls CreateProcessA with that executable, the current command line plus the two flags, inheritable handles and the original working directory. It stores the new process handle in child_handle_ (the object owns it; the thread handle is closed at once), calls set_spawned(true) and returns OVERSEE_TEST. Each GTEST_DEATH_TEST_CHECK_ (CreatePipe, event creation, the GetModuleFileNameA comparison, CreateProcessA) calls DeathTestAbort, which writes the message to stderr and aborts (or, if the internal flag were set, exits with status 1), so on those failures AssumeRole does not return. The function returns only EXECUTE_TEST or OVERSEE_TEST, never TEST_FAILED. The GetModuleFileNameA check compares against _MAX_PATH + 1, a value that call cannot return when given size _MAX_PATH, so it neither detects truncation nor a zero (failure) return.
note: reviewer RIGHT on both round-15 claims: buffer is _MAX_PATH+1 but size argument is _MAX_PATH (lines 792-795); child process handle is owned by child_handle_.Reset (line 825). Also reviewer round-1 claim (never TEST_FAILED) is right

name: ParseNaturalNumber
prose: template <typename Integer> bool ParseNaturalNumber(const ::std::string& str, Integer* number) (gtest-internal-inl.h, compiled only when GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST; slice shows only the tail, head at line 1022). Precondition: number is a valid, writable Integer pointer (it is written only on success); sizeof(Integer) must be <= sizeof(unsigned long long), otherwise GTEST_CHECK_ logs a fatal error and aborts, and that check runs after strtoull has been called. Postcondition: returns false without touching *number if str is empty or its first character is not a decimal digit (so a sign or leading whitespace is rejected). Otherwise errno is set to 0, str is parsed with strtoull in base 10, and the function returns true and stores the converted value in *number only if the whole string was consumed (*end == '\0'), errno is still 0 (no ERANGE), and converting the parsed value to Integer and back to unsigned long long gives the same value; in every other case it returns false and leaves *number unchanged. Side effect: errno is modified.
note: slice cut head; old prose wrongly said an empty string parses as 0 and returns true; lines 1023-1029 return false for empty/non-digit start

name: AtomMatchesChar
prose: bool AtomMatchesChar(bool escaped, char pattern_char, char ch) (gtest-port.cc line 781, part of the simple regex engine used when GTEST_USES_SIMPLE_RE is defined). Pure function. If escaped is true it switches on pattern_char: 'd' returns whether ch is '0'-'9'; 'D' the negation; 'f', 'n', 'r', 't', 'v' return whether ch equals form feed, newline, carriage return, tab, vertical tab respectively; 's' returns whether ch is one of space, \f, \n, \r, \t, \v (and is never true for ch == '\0'); 'S' the negation of that; 'w' returns whether ch is an ASCII letter, digit or '_'; 'W' the negation. For any other pattern_char with escaped true it returns true only if pattern_char is one of the 32 ASCII punctuation characters listed in IsAsciiPunct and pattern_char == ch. If escaped is false it returns true when pattern_char == '.' and ch != '\n', or when pattern_char == ch. The result for an invalid atom is documented in the source as undefined, but the code has no failure path and always falls through to one of these returns. No state is read or written.

name: TestRepeatWithFilterForFailedTests
prose: void TestRepeatWithFilterForFailedTests(int repeat) (gtest_repeat_test.cc lines 180-193). Precondition: repeat >= 1 for the checks to hold. The function sets the repeat flag to repeat, recreate_environments_when_repeating to true and the test filter to "*ShouldFail", then ResetCounts() zeroes all counters and registers a new MyEnvironment. For repeat == 0 RUN_ALL_TESTS runs no iteration and the first check (expecting 1) fails; for a negative repeat the tests repeat without end (per the source comment), so the function does not finish. Postcondition for repeat >= 1: RUN_ALL_TESTS() returns 1 (FooTest.ShouldFail fails on every iteration), and the counters equal g_environment_set_up_count == repeat, g_environment_tear_down_count == repeat, g_should_fail_count == repeat, g_should_pass_count == 0, g_death_test_count == 0 and g_param_test_count == 0. Each check is GTEST_CHECK_INT_EQ_, which on a mismatch prints Value of/Actual/Expected/Which is to stdout and calls posix::Abort(); the function otherwise returns nothing. It leaves the repeat, recreate_environments and filter flags set.
note: reviewer RIGHT: 'repeat any int' wrong (repeat<=0); the earlier reviewer claim (setup/teardown == repeat) was already reflected
